name: Customer due diligence programme
description: End-to-end identity verification, beneficial-ownership resolution and risk classification at onboarding, with periodic refresh cycles keyed to customer risk.
purpose: Verify who the customer is, who owns it and how risky it is, at onboarding and on refresh.

name: Enhanced due diligence track
description: Escalation lane for high-risk relationships: senior-management approval, source-of-wealth/funds evidence, tightened monitoring thresholds, PEP and high-risk-country handling.
purpose: Apply heightened scrutiny and senior sign-off to customers and transactions the risk assessment flags as high risk.

name: Business-wide risk assessment
description: Documented, periodically refreshed assessment of ML/TF exposure across customers, geographies, products, transactions and channels; feeds thresholds used by other blocks.
purpose: A documented, board-approved assessment of the money-laundering and terrorist-financing risks the business faces.

name: AML governance & internal controls
description: Policies, controls and procedures proportionate to the risk assessment: MLRO appointment, screening of relevant employees, independent audit where warranted.
purpose: A nominated officer / MLRO function with the authority, independence and reporting line to run the AML programme.

name: Records & retention regime
description: Unified retention schedule and retrieval capability covering CDD records, transaction data and processing-activity records, with defensible deletion at end of retention.
purpose: Keep the records the regime demands, retrievable for the required period and disposed of after it.

name: Privacy-by-design pipeline
description: Lawful-basis register, DPIA workflow triggered from product intake, DPO designation, and privacy review gates embedded in the delivery process.
purpose: Build data-protection requirements into every processing activity from design onwards.

name: Breach & incident response (72h-capable)
description: Single incident pipeline that classifies personal-data breaches and ICT incidents, drives containment, and hits the GDPR 72-hour and DORA major-incident reporting clocks.
purpose: Detect, assess, contain and notify personal-data and security incidents within the statutory windows.

name: Information security baseline
description: Core technical control set: account management, least privilege, audit logging, configuration baselines, vulnerability scanning and continuous monitoring.
purpose: The minimum technical and organisational security measures the organisation must run.

name: ICT resilience & third-party register
description: DORA-grade operational resilience: ICT risk framework owned by the management body, register of ICT third-party arrangements, concentration analysis and exit plans.
purpose: The register of ICT third parties and the resilience arrangements the regime requires.

name: Client asset safeguarding (crypto)
description: Segregation of client crypto-assets and funds, custody policy, key-management ceremony, and daily reconciliation against client entitlement records.
purpose: Client assets held and segregated so they are safeguarded and returnable.

name: Promotional claims review
description: Every promotional claim, including a paid endorser's post, is checked before publication: it reflects the endorser's honest experience, performance claims are substantiated and typical, and nothing in it is deceptive.
purpose: Stop deceptive or unsubstantiated claims before an endorser publishes them.

name: Material connection disclosure standard
description: The written standard for how a paid or otherwise connected endorser states the relationship: clearly and conspicuously, in the same medium as the endorsement, including compensation for a promoter.
purpose: Make every material connection and every paid endorsement visible to the audience.

name: Written promoter agreement and oversight
description: A written agreement with each compensated promoter, approved by a compliance role, and the adviser's oversight of that promoter's testimonials and endorsements.
purpose: Bind each paid promoter to the adviser's marketing obligations and keep the approval on record.

name: Expert and organisation endorsement qualification
description: When an endorser is presented as an expert or as an organisation, the endorser's qualifications and the organisation's collective judgment are verified before use.
purpose: Use expert or organisation endorsements only when the claimed expertise or collective judgment is real.
